Theme

Philosophy quotes about understanding

Understanding appears in this archive as a live philosophical concern—not a slogan. These verified English passages show how thinkers treat understanding as a problem of judgment, practice, or explanation.

12 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

Why this theme matters

Across 4 recurring voices here (notably G. W. F. Hegel and Baruch Spinoza), understanding is framed through German Idealism and Rationalism. Some passages define understanding; others warn how it fails; still others relocate it inside habit, community, or language.

In the history of philosophy

Discussions of understanding travel through European modern and modern European traditions. Compare the quotations below with their school labels rather than forcing a single definition.

Thinkers in this collection

Ludwig Wittgenstein , G. W. F. Hegel , Ralph Waldo Emerson , Baruch Spinoza , Søren Kierkegaard , Anselm of Canterbury , Laozi , Hannah Arendt

Frequently asked questions

What did philosophers say about understanding?

They disagreed in productive ways. In this archive, G. W. F. Hegel, Baruch Spinoza, and related voices treat understanding as something to clarify, cultivate, or critique—not merely to celebrate.

Where can I find philosophy quotes about understanding?

This theme page gathers 10 verified English quotations tagged Understanding, with links to thinkers and sources.

How should I read quotes about understanding?

Read the sentence, then check school and source. A compact line is an entry point into an argument about understanding, not a substitute for the surrounding text.

  1. My propositions are elucidatory in this way: he who understands me finally recognizes them as nonsensical…He must surmount these propositions; then he sees the world rightly.
    Ludwig Wittgenstein
    Analytic Philosophy
  2. The owl of Minerva spreads its wings only with the falling of the dusk.
    G. W. F. Hegel
    German Idealism
  3. What is rational is actual; and what is actual is rational.
    G. W. F. Hegel
    German Idealism
  4. To be great is to be misunderstood.
    Ralph Waldo Emerson
    Transcendentalism
  5. I shall endeavor not to laugh at human actions, nor to weep over them, nor to hate them, but to understand them.
    Baruch Spinoza
    Rationalism
  6. It is quite true what philosophy says, that life must be understood backwards. But then one forgets the other principle: that it must be lived forwards.
    Søren Kierkegaard
    Existentialism
  7. I do not seek to understand so that I may believe, but I believe so that I may understand.
    Anselm of Canterbury
    Scholasticism
  8. Not to laugh at, lament, or detest human actions, but to understand them.
    Baruch Spinoza
    Rationalism
  9. Those who understand me are few; therefore I am valued.
    Laozi
    Daoism
  10. Storytelling reveals meaning without committing the error of defining it.
    Hannah Arendt
    Political Phenomenology
  11. If the apparent sense of a scriptural text conflicts with demonstration, that apparent sense admits of allegorical interpretation.
    Averroes
    Islamic Philosophy
  12. Religion cannot be fully understood either within the parameters of utility or from a sociological viewpoint alone.
    Nishitani Keiji
    Kyoto School
